b2plus-past-unreal.title: Past Unreal Conditional: -gan bo'lsa edi / -gan bo'lardi
b2plus-past-unreal.explanation: To talk about a past that didn't happen, Uzbek combines the -gan participle with bo'lsa edi in the "if" clause and bo'lardi (the conditional of bo'lmoq) in the result: agar bilganimda edi, kelmagan bo'lardim (if I had known, I wouldn't have come).
b2plus-past-unreal.fact: Every piece of this construction is independently familiar from earlier levels (-gan, edi, -sa, bo'lmoq) -- B2+ fluency here is less about learning new suffixes and more about correctly stacking four already-known ones in the right order.

dialogue.native: Agar u yerda bo'lganingizda, nima qilardingiz?
dialogue.en: If you had been there, what would you have done?

b2plus-emphatic-ku.title: Emphatic Particle: -ku
b2plus-emphatic-ku.explanation: -ku attaches to the end of a clause to add assertive emphasis, roughly "you know" or "after all": men aytdim-ku! (I did tell you!/I told you, didn't I!). It signals the speaker feels the point should already be obvious or agreed on.
b2plus-emphatic-ku.fact: -ku carries a faintly argumentative or exasperated tone -- it's the grammatical equivalent of raising your eyebrows while saying something, and overusing it in formal writing reads as oddly confrontational.

dialogue.en: I did tell you, you just didn't listen!

b2plus-axir.title: Discourse Marker: axir
b2plus-axir.explanation: Axir ("after all/but") opens a clause that reminds the listener of something relevant they seem to have overlooked: axir men senga aytgandim (after all, I did tell you), axir u hali yosh (but he/she is still young, after all).
b2plus-axir.fact: Axir and -ku often appear in the very same sentence for double emphasis (axir aytdim-ku!, "but I DID tell you, after all!") -- Uzbek stacks its emphatic markers rather than treating them as mutually exclusive alternatives.

dialogue.en: But this sounds very strange, after all.

b2plus-converb-chain.title: Converb Chains: -ib
b2plus-converb-chain.explanation: The converb -ib links a sequence of actions by the same subject into one flowing sentence, with only the LAST verb carrying full tense marking: turib, kiyinib, ishga bordim (I got up, got dressed, and went to work) -- literally "getting up, getting dressed, I-went to work".
b2plus-converb-chain.fact: Only the final verb in the chain shows person and tense at all -- turib and kiyinib are grammatically bare converbs, not separate finite verbs -- so a very long chain of actions can rest on a single tensed verb at the very end of the sentence.

dialogue.en: What did you do in the evening?
I ate, read a book, and went to sleep.

b2plus-double-negative.title: Emphatic Double Negative: -may qolmaydi
b2plus-double-negative.pattern: [verb stem] + -may qolmaydi (won't fail to ~ / is bound to ~)
b2plus-double-negative.explanation: Combining the negative converb -may with qolmaydi ("won't remain/stay") produces a strong positive claim through double negation: u kelmay qolmaydi (he/she won't fail to come = he/she is bound to come).
b2plus-double-negative.fact: The two negatives (-may and qol-may-di's own negative) don't cancel out to plain neutral certainty -- they combine into something stronger and more emphatic than the simple affirmative u albatta keladi would sound, similar to how English "won't NOT come" reads as more forceful than a flat "will come".

dialogue.en: I wonder if he/she will come to the meeting.
Of course he'll/she'll come, he/she is bound to.

items.en: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.

items.uz: Agar vaqtim bo'lganida, sizga yordam bergan bo'lardim.
items.en: If I had had time, I would have helped you.

items.uz: U ogohlantirilganida edi, bu xato yuz bermagan bo'lardi.
items.en: If he/she had been warned, this mistake wouldn't have happened.

items.uz: Agar bu haqda oldinroq bilganimda, boshqacha qaror qabul qilgan bo'lardim.
items.en: If I had known about this earlier, I would have made a different decision.
If you hadn't been late, you would have caught the train.

items.uz: Agar u yordam so'raganida, biz albatta bergan bo'lardik.
items.en: If he/she had asked for help, we would have definitely given it.

items.uz: Agar bu imkoniyatni qo'ldan boy bermaganimda, hayotim boshqacha bo'lgan bo'lardi.
items.en: If I hadn't missed this opportunity, my life would have been different.

items.uz: Agar u meni tinglaganida, bu muammo yuzaga kelmagan bo'lardi.
items.en: If he/she had listened to me, this problem wouldn't have arisen.

items.uz: Agar ko'proq mashq qilganimda, imtihonni yaxshiroq topshirgan bo'lardim.
items.en: If I had practiced more, I would have done better on the exam.

items.uz: Agar siz kelmaganingizda, tadbir boshqacha o'tgan bo'lardi.
items.en: If you hadn't come, the event would have gone differently.

items.uz: Agar bu qaror to'g'ri bo'lganida, natija boshqacha bo'lardi.
items.en: If this decision had been correct, the result would have been different.

items.uz: Agar u sabr qilganida, hammasi yaxshi tugagan bo'lardi.
items.en: If he/she had been patient, everything would have ended well.
I did tell you!
This is very easy, you know!
He/she has come, you see!
I know, don't worry!
This isn't right, is it!
You've forgotten, haven't you!
We don't have time, you know!
We resolved this issue, didn't we!
He/she is still young, after all!
This is very expensive, you know!
I trusted you, you know!
This job isn't hard, is it!
But I did tell you, after all.
But he/she is still young, after all.
After all, this is a very important matter.
After all, we all make mistakes.
After all, time waits for no one.
But you did promise, after all.
After all, this is our duty.
After all, he/she is my friend.
After all, this is the truth.
After all, we work together.
After all, this decision depends on you.
After all, nothing comes easy.
I got up, got dressed, and went to work.
He/she came, sat down, and drank tea.
I ate, read a book, and went to sleep.

items.uz: Xat yozib, uni jo'natib, dam oldim.
items.en: I wrote a letter, sent it, and rested.
He/she came running and delivered the message.
I washed the clothes, dried them, and folded them.
He/she stood up and started speaking.

items.uz: Uyni tozalab, ovqat pishirib, mehmonlarni kutib oldim.
items.en: I cleaned the house, cooked food, and welcomed the guests.
He/she took the book and flipped through the pages.
He/she stopped the car, got out, and looked around.
I finished the work and submitted the report.

items.uz: U kulib, hazil qilib, hammani xursand qildi.
items.en: He/she laughed, joked, and made everyone happy.
He/she is bound to come.
This plan is bound to be realized.
He/she is bound to know about this.
Things are bound to go well.

items.uz: Vaqt kelib, hammasi oshkor bo'lmay qolmaydi.
items.en: In time, everything is bound to come to light.
He/she is bound to keep his/her word.
Hard work is bound to give results.
This mistake is bound to repeat.
The truth is bound to come out sooner or later.
He/she is bound to hear this.
Such patience is bound to be rewarded.
Kindness is bound not to be forgotten.
